```{r setup}
#| include: false
# Figures and tables come from npn_fire/scripts/90_nf_figs.R (figs/<figure>_<profile>.png +
# manifest.csv; tables/*.csv). Everything on this page is summarised to EPA Level II ecoregions.
figs <- if (file.exists("figs/manifest.csv")) {
  utils::read.csv("figs/manifest.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
} else data.frame(figure = character(), profile = character())

show_fig <- function(name, caption, alt = caption) {
  m <- figs[figs$figure == name, , drop = FALSE]
  pick <- intersect(c("full", "dev"), m$profile)
  pick <- pick[file.exists(sprintf("figs/%s_%s.png", name, pick))]
  if (!length(pick)) {
    cat(sprintf('\n::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}\n## Figure pending\n%s\n:::\n\n', caption))
    return(invisible())
  }
  r <- m[m$profile == pick[1], ][1, ]
  note <- sprintf("[%s &middot; %s &middot; figure made %s]{.fig-meta}", r$extent, r$years, r$made)
  cat(sprintf('\n![%s %s](figs/%s_%s.png){#fig-%s fig-alt="%s" .column-page-right}\n\n',
              caption, note, name, pick[1], gsub("_", "-", name), alt))
}
tab <- function(f) { p <- file.path("tables", f); if (file.exists(p)) utils::read.csv(p, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE) else NULL }
fmt <- function(x, d = 0) format(round(x, d), big.mark = ",", nsmall = d, trim = TRUE)
RY <- tab("nf_record_years.csv"); GR <- tab("nf_groups.csv"); INV <- tab("nf_inventory_sites.csv")
n_rec <- if (!is.null(RY)) fmt(sum(RY$records) / 1e6, 1) else "29.4"
n_py <- if (!is.null(RY)) fmt(sum(RY$plant_years) / 1e6, 2) else "1.38"
n_ok <- if (!is.null(RY)) fmt(sum(RY$usable_onsets)) else "409,000"
yr_rng <- if (!is.null(RY)) paste0(min(RY$year), "&ndash;", max(RY$year)) else "2009&ndash;2024"
```

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
## Work in progress
This page is updated as the analysis runs. Results are preliminary and will change. The study stands
on its own (its own data, units and code). Related pages: the [NPN grass curing study](npn_study.html),
the [fire activity study](fire_study.html) (satellite curing and fire in six pilot regions) and the
[fuel phenology regions](index.html).
:::

## At a glance

**The question.** Do the seasons that USA National Phenology Network (NPN) observers record on the
ground (leaf-out, flowering, leaf color and leaf fall, grass and forb green-up and drying) line up with
when fire seasons open and close? Where the record is deep enough, do early and late phenology years
shift fire activity? And, as a result in its own right: **where across the contiguous U.S. do NPN
observations and fire activity overlap** in place, season and year, so that NPN could inform wildfire
management, and where would more monitoring help?

**Why it matters.** Fire managers judge live fuels by eye and by fixed calendars; satellite and
weather indices stand in for plants that are rarely observed. NPN is the largest ground record of plant
seasons in the country, collected by volunteers, partner organizations and NEON. Its value for fire has
not been assessed across fuel types and regions. This study does that with the fire records already
assembled for the project.

**Approach, simplest first.**

1. **Where they align (inventory).** NPN sites and usable dates by EPA Level II ecoregion, plant group,
   phenophase and year; fire activity by ecoregion, fuel type, week and year. Where do both exist in the
   same seasons and years? This decides which tests below are possible anywhere.
2. **Seasonal alignment.** In each ecoregion, does the weekly fire curve in a fuel type change at the
   typical date of the matching phenophase (e.g. fewer fires in deciduous forest after leaf-out), beyond
   the seasonal cycle of dryness?
3. **Year to year, where the record allows.** In ecoregions with enough sites each year, does an early
   or late phenology year shift fire activity after a dryness baseline? Expected to be possible in only a
   few places; reported as feasibility and as the monitoring it would take.

**No satellite phenology** is used: this is a test of the ground record. Satellite fire detections
appear only as a fire outcome.

**Status (`r format(Sys.Date(), "%B %-d, %Y")`).** The NPN record is downloaded and cleaned
(`r n_rec` million status records, `r yr_rng`), plants are grouped, and fire activity is tabulated by
ecoregion and fuel type. Next: the dryness baseline, then the inventory (step 1).

## Data and methods

### Data

- **NPN observations.** Every plant status and intensity record for the contiguous U.S., 2009–2024
  (the Nature's Notebook era), downloaded from the NPN data service. On each visit an observer records,
  for a tagged plant and each of its phenophases, whether the phase is present (yes / no) and, for many
  phases, how much (an intensity class: percent of the canopy full, percent of leaves colored, percent
  of a grass still green, or counts of buds, flowers and fruits). All plant groups are included,
  conifers too; animals are not. NEON (National Ecological Observatory Network) records are part of the
  same data set and are tracked separately.
- **Plant groups.** NPN's functional type gives grasses, forbs, conifers and cacti. Broadleaf woody
  species are split into trees and shrubs from USDA PLANTS growth habit; species PLANTS lists as both
  are split by mature height (20 ft and taller: tree). The 30 most-observed species still unresolved
  (cultivars, genus-only names, desert trees) were assigned by hand.
- **Fire.** Three records assembled for the [fire activity study](fire_study.html):
  **FPA-FOD** (7th edition), wildfire starts of all sizes 2001–2024 with debris and open burning removed;
  **MTBS** large-fire perimeters (wildfire and wildland fire use) 2001–2024 (2024 not yet complete);
  **VIIRS** 375 m active-fire detections 2012–2024 linked to reported wildfires, with cropland and
  unlinked detections removed.
- **Fuels.** LANDFIRE 2023 fire behavior fuel models (Scott and Burgan 40), grouped into grass,
  grass-shrub, shrub, timber-understory, timber litter and slash, as shares of each 4 km cell.
- **Units.** EPA / CEC Level II ecoregions (CEC 1997); Level III as a check where the record is dense.
- **Weather.** PRISM daily precipitation and temperature, for a 60-day water balance (precipitation
  minus potential evapotranspiration) as the dryness baseline (in progress).

### Methods

- **Dates.** For each tagged plant, phenophase and year: the **onset** is the first "yes" and the
  **end** the last "yes". An onset counts as *usable* when the previous visit, at most 14 days before,
  recorded "no" (7- and 30-day versions as checks); the same rule applies to ends. Phenophases are
  grouped across NPN protocols into NPN's 13 plant phenophase classes (initial growth, young leaves,
  leaves, colored leaves, falling leaves, flowers, open flowers, pollen, end of flowering, fruits,
  unripe fruits, ripe fruits, fruit drop).
- **Intensity dates.** Percent classes are converted to their midpoints (a "no" counts as 0 %). Two
  dates per plant-year: the first reading at or above 50 % (e.g. canopy half full) and the first
  reading below 50 % after the season's peak (e.g. a grass half cured). NPN intensity starts in 2011.
- **Cleaning.** Uncertain readings are dropped; repeat visits on one day are merged (yes if any
  observer said yes; highest intensity). Sites whose coordinates fall outside the contiguous U.S. or
  far from any ecoregion are left out of the ecoregion tables.
- **Year departures** (step 3) will be measured from each plant's own typical date and averaged to
  the ecoregion and year, weighting sites, not plants, so that changes in who observes don't read as
  changes in the plants.
- **Fire by fuel type.** Each fire is split over the LANDFIRE fuel-group shares of its 4 km cell (MTBS:
  of every burned cell, by burned area). Plant groups are matched to fuel groups in step 1 (deciduous
  and conifer trees with timber fuels, shrubs with shrub fuels, grasses and forbs with grass fuels).
  Weeks are fixed 7-day blocks from January 1, as in the fire activity study.
- **Which fire record leads** is set before any test is run: in each ecoregion and fuel type, the
  outcome with the best coverage in the inventory is reported first, the others as checks.

## The NPN record

The download holds `r n_rec` million plant status records from `r yr_rng`. Cleaned to one row per plant,
phenophase and year, that is `r n_py` million plant-years, of which `r n_ok` have a usable onset. The
record grew quickly after 2011 and has held at about 15,000 plants a year since 2017, while the number
of sites peaked in 2020–21 and has fallen since: fewer sites, observed more often.

```{r fig-record}
#| results: asis
show_fig("nf_record", "The NPN plant record by year: status records, plants observed (with the range of sites a year) and usable onsets.")
```

```{r fig-groups}
#| results: asis
show_fig("nf_groups", "Usable onsets by plant group, split by kind of phenophase. Deciduous trees dominate the record; grasses, the fuel the other studies centre on, are a small part.")
```

```{r tbl-groups}
#| tbl-cap: "Usable onsets by plant group and kind of phenophase, all years."
if (!is.null(GR)) {
  d <- GR[order(-GR$total), c("label", "Leaves", "Flowers", "Fruits", "total")]
  names(d) <- c("Plant group", "Leaves", "Flowers", "Fruits", "Total")
  for (k in 2:5) d[[k]] <- fmt(d[[k]])
  knitr::kable(d, row.names = FALSE, align = "lrrrr")
}
```

## Where the record is

Sites with at least one usable leaf-out-type onset (initial growth, young leaves or leaves), by
ecoregion and plant group, over the whole record:

```{r fig-effort-map}
#| results: asis
show_fig("nf_effort_map", "Level II ecoregions shaded by the number of sites with a usable leaf-out-type onset, per plant group (numbers shown where 5 or more).")
```

Deciduous trees and shrubs are observed almost everywhere, and densely across the East. Conifers and
evergreen shrubs have a moderate record in the West and Northeast. Grasses are thin everywhere, with no
more than about 20 sites in any ecoregion over the whole record, the same limit the
[NPN grass curing study](npn_study.html) found.

Year-to-year tests need sites every year, not only over the whole record:

```{r fig-effort-years}
#| results: asis
show_fig("nf_effort_years", "Sites with a usable onset of any kind, by ecoregion and year. The NPN curing study found that about 10 sites give a reliable regional mean for a year.")
```

```{r tbl-inventory}
#| tbl-cap: "Sites with a usable leaf-out-type onset by ecoregion and plant group, whole record (ecoregions with 20 or more sites in a group)."
if (!is.null(INV)) {
  lab <- c(deciduous_tree = "Decid. tree", deciduous_shrub = "Decid. shrub", conifer = "Conifer", evergreen_shrub = "Evergr. shrub",
           grass = "Grass", forb = "Forb", evergreen_tree = "Evergr. tree", other = "Other")
  W <- stats::reshape(INV[, c("eco_l2_code", "eco_l2_name", "group", "sites")], idvar = c("eco_l2_code", "eco_l2_name"), timevar = "group", direction = "wide")
  names(W) <- sub("^sites\\.", "", names(W))
  cols <- intersect(names(lab), names(W)); W[cols][is.na(W[cols])] <- 0
  W <- W[apply(W[cols], 1, max) >= 20, ]
  o <- order(as.numeric(sub("\\..*", "", W$eco_l2_code)), as.numeric(sub("^\\d+\\.", "", W$eco_l2_code))); W <- W[o, ]
  nm <- gsub("\\bUsa\\b", "USA", tools::toTitleCase(tolower(W$eco_l2_name)))
  d <- data.frame(Ecoregion = paste(W$eco_l2_code, nm), W[cols], check.names = FALSE)
  names(d)[-1] <- lab[cols]
  knitr::kable(d, row.names = FALSE)
}
```

```{r fig-fire}
#| results: asis
show_fig("nf_fire_fuel", "Fire activity per year by ecoregion, split by LANDFIRE fuel group: FPA-FOD wildfires of all sizes (2001&ndash;2024) and VIIRS active-fire pixel-days (2012&ndash;2024).")
```

## Next steps

1. **Dryness baseline:** the 60-day PRISM water balance by ecoregion and day, and its weekly climatology.
2. **Inventory (step 1):** match plant groups to fuel groups and count, for each ecoregion, plant group
   and phenophase, the years and weeks where usable NPN dates and fires coincide; pick the lead fire
   record for each.
3. **Seasonal alignment (step 2)** wherever the inventory allows it; **year to year (step 3)** in the
   few ecoregions with enough sites each year.

## Decisions

| Date | Decision |
|---|---|
| Oct 25 | A separate study of NPN's potential for wildfire applications across CONUS, without satellite phenology |
| Oct 31 | All NPN plant status and intensity records (conifers included, no animals); EPA Level II ecoregions; evaluate FPA-FOD, MTBS and VIIRS; self-contained code |
| Nov 1 | Broadleaf trees vs shrubs from USDA PLANTS growth habit, then mature height (20 ft); 30 species by hand |
| Nov 1 | LANDFIRE fuel groups as the fuel layer; FPA-FOD all sizes and 10 acres and up; VIIRS from the fire study's CONUS-wide screen |
